name: IspcTextureCompressor

source.verification: GitHub HTTPS commit archive of the vendor repository (head of master = 79ddbc90334fc31edd438e68ccb0fe99b4e15aab, the archival notice of 2024-09-23), downloaded on 2026-11-27 and its SHA-256 recorded. Upstream publishes no releases, signatures or hashes, so it is pinned by the commit and the archive hash. kernel.ispc (before Rocks.patch), ispc_texcomp.cpp and ispc_texcomp.h are byte-identical to the copy UE 5.8 ships (Engine/Source/ThirdParty/Intel/ISPCTexComp/ISPCTextureCompressor-14d998c); the later upstream commits only change kernel_astc.ispc, readme.md and the license text. Imported files are license.txt and the BC6H/BC7 encoder sources ispc_texcomp/kernel.ispc, ispc_texcomp/ispc_texcomp.cpp and ispc_texcomp/ispc_texcomp.h (the ASTC sources, the sample application, project files and prebuilt ISPC compiler are not imported).

licenses.upstreamExpression: license.txt (MIT, Copyright 2017 Intel Corporation); the source headers carry the same MIT text (Copyright (c) 2016-2019, Intel Corporation)

notes: BC6H and BC7 encoder of the texture cook (Docs/Design/AssetSystem section 12.17.6, stage TC3b) — the encoder UE 5.8 TextureFormatIntelISPCTexComp uses. UE links a prebuilt DLL compiled with --target=sse2,sse4,avx,avx2 --opt=fast-math; Rocks compiles kernel.ispc with the pinned ISPC (Build/Toolchain.json ispc) for one target per architecture with FMA and fast-math off (Docs/Design/BuildTargets section 3.12), so the output bytes do not depend on the host CPU. Compared with UE by quality (PSNR), not bytes (TC3c).

Only the BC6H and BC7 entry points are used (TextureTools TextureBlockEncode; Programs/TextureCodecCompare uses the ispc_texcomp.h types to call the UE DLL). The BC1-BC5 and ETC1 entry points compile with the kernel but are not called (BC1-BC5 is the NVTT port, TC1). The ASTC declarations of ispc_texcomp.h have no definition here (ASTC is astc-encoder, TC4).

The x64 build runs the SSE4 target, so the caller checks SSE4.2 before the first call (TextureBlockEncode returns Unsupported without it). The kernel follows the caller's FTZ/DAZ state; the caller runs it in the deterministic floating point environment.
Android targets do not build this library (ISPC sources are desktop-only — BuildTargets BD46); TextureTools depends on it only for Windows and macOS.

modifications.reason: compute_axis restarts the power iteration from the covariance column with the largest diagonal when the result is provably not the principal axis (Rayleigh quotient below half of trace/channels — half so that an isotropic covariance, a solid block, never restarts on one ulp of rounding). Upstream starts from {1,1,1,1} only; with the exact IEEE build (no fast-math, no FMA — Docs/Design/BuildTargets section 3.12) a principal axis orthogonal to that vector, such as R rising and G falling by the same steps, stays orthogonal and BC7 quality drops (TC3c measured 37.7 dB against UE 49.9 dB on the negative-correlation test image; UE escapes only through fast-math or FMA rounding). Blocks that never restart keep the upstream bytes (Docs/Design/AssetSystem section 12.17.6 item 10).
